citation: Singh, Aggarwal, Rajivan & Gonzalez (2019) — Training to Detect Phishing Emails: Effects of the Frequency of Experienced Phishing Emails, HFES Annual Meeting

source.note: v1 port uses the actual 239-email Singh et al. (2019) stimulus set (PhishingDataset_HFES2019.csv on OSF: 186 phishing + 53 ham). Emails are rendered with realistic email-client styling (header pane + HTML body) so the visual surface matches what a real participant sees in their inbox. Training-phase feedback follows Singh's outcome-feedback condition (correct/incorrect after each response, no detail). The task drops Singh's incentive and detail-feedback conditions to keep the v1 paradigm focused on the basic learn-from-feedback signature.

description: Classify emails as legitimate (ham) or phishing across three phases. Pre-training (10 trials, no feedback), training (40 trials with outcome feedback), post-training (10 trials, no feedback). Tests above-chance discrimination, training-induced improvement, and learning-from-feedback dynamics.
